SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES– SELECTION OF FIRMS)

 

UGANDA RURAL ROADS PROGRAM

PROJECT ID: P182056

Procurement Reference No. MoWT/CONS/2025-2026/00502

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: Consultancy Services for Feasibility Study for the DUCAR (District, Urban and Community Access Roads) network, Bridges and Drainage Structures in 77 District Local Governments:

 

The Government of the Republic of Uganda represented by the Ministry of Works and Transport (MoWT) has received a grant of US$4,500,000 from the World Bank towards the Preparation of the Rural Roads Program and intends to apply part of the proceeds for undertaking Consultancy Services for Feasibility Study for the DUCAR network, Bridges and Drainage Structures in 77 District Local Governments. The project is spread across the 5 regions of the Country, and as such, 5 lots have been formulated as summarized below:

  1. LOT 1-West Nile Region; 12 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Adjumani, Arua, Koboko, Madi Okollo, Maracha, Moyo, Nebbi, Obongi, Pakwach, Terego, Yumbe and Zombo.
  2. LOT 2-Northern Region; 14 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Agago, Alebtong, Amolatar, Amuru, Apach, Gulu, Kitgum, Kole, Lamwo, Lira, Nwoya, Omoro, Otuke and Oyam.
  3. LOT 3-Western Region; 18 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Bundibugyo, Bushenyi, Isingiro, Kabarole, Kakumiro, Kamwenge, Kanungu, Kasese, Kibaale, Kiryandongo, Kisoro, Kitagwenda, Kyegegwa, Masindi, Mitooma, Ntoroko, Rukungiri and Sheema
  4. LOT 4-Eastern Region; 23 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Amuria, Bududa, Bugiri, Bukedea, Bukwo, Bulambuli, Busia, Butaleja, Iganga, Kaliro, Kamuli, Katakwi, Kibuuku, Kumi, Kween, Manafwa, Nabilatuk, Namayingo, Namutumba, Ngora, Pallisa, Serere and Sironko
  5. LOT 5-Central Region; 10 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Buikwe, Butambala, Kalangala, Kayunga, Luwero, Mukono, Nakasongola, Rakai, Sembabule and Wakiso

The Consulting Services (“the Services”) are to be provided with the following objectives;

  1. Undertake Detailed Engineering Designs, determine an Environment and Social Management Plan, and prepare bidding documents for 1,100km of the DUCAR network, 240 bridges and drainage structures, and 50km of swamps raising in 77 District Local Governments;
  2. Undertake Economic and Financial Assessment for 1,100km of the DUCAR network, 240 bridges and drainage structures, and 50km of swamps improvement in 77 District Local Governments; and
  3. Generate a Feasibility study report for 1,100km of the DUCAR network, 240 bridges and drainage structures, and 50km of swamps in 77 District Local Governments.

The implementation period of the assignment is 6 (six) Calendar Months from the time of contract signing.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be assessed at www.mowt.go.ug.

The Ministry of Works and Transport now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

The successful execution of this consultancy requires a Consultant with extensive experience, technical competence, and proven ability to work within government and donor-funded project environments. The Consultant should combine strong analytical and facilitation skills with contextual knowledge of Uganda’s transport sector to ensure that the assessment is both practical and implementable. Specifically, the Consultant is expected to meet the following minimum requirements:

  1. Must have completed projects with a total of 100km or more for Design or Construction Supervision of Highways or Urban roads in the last 10 years;

(ii)    Experience in working with Government and Donor-funded projects; and

(iii)   Strong skills in Analysis, Reporting, and Facilitation.

 

N.B:  

  1. Firms should not bid in more than 2 (two) lots.
  2. Individual experts’ bio-data is not required at this stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”  dated February 2025 (“Procurement in Investment Project Financing: Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications in the form of Joint Venture and/or Lead / Sub Consultancy. Consultants shall indicate whether the association is a Joint Venture and/or Sub-Consultancy. In the case of a Joint Venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”  dated February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”)

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. (Monday to Friday, 08 00 hours to 17 00hours, except on public holidays).

 

Expressions of Interest (One Original plus three (3) copies must be delivered in a written form to the address in person or by email on or before February 26, 2026 at 11 00Hrs local time.  The package must be clearly marked “Expression of Interest for Consultancy Services for Feasibility Study for the DUCAR network, Bridges and Drainage Structures in 77 District Local Governments”.

Kampala, Uganda

The Procuring and Disposing Entity shall conduct a public opening of Expression of Interest at 11 30Hrs local time on March 06, 2026.

Invitations for Expression of Interest

Assignment Title:

Assistant Statistician (Tourism Statistics)

Name of Project:

Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in Tonga (SICBT

Grant No:

D543-TO

Date of Issuance:

Monday, 2nd March 2026

Market Approach:

Open for Tongan Nationals Only

Due date/time for Expression of Interest (EOI): Friday, 13th March 2026, no later than 4:30 pm local time.

The Government of Tonga has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Tonga Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building (SICBT) Project. It intends to apply part of the proceeds to the recruitment of an Assistant Statistician (Tourism Statistics).

The objective of this assignment is to recruit an Assistant Statistician (Tourism Statistics) to support the execution of field-level data collection, manage survey logistics, and facilitate inter-agency coordination. The Assistant will be responsible for gathering the raw data required to populate the TSA framework and support the TSD Economics Division.

  • Duration: Short-term position for 6 months, including a 1-month probationary period.
  • Tentative Start Date: 18 March 2026.
  • Location: The Assistant will be based at the TSD office in Nuku’alofa, Tonga.

The Assistant Statistician (Tourism Statistics) will provide essential support to the Economics Division, including:

  • Execute surveys to capture a comprehensive view of the sector, including but not limited to Accommodation Surveys, Maritime Tourism, e.g., conducting Yacht and Cruise Ship surveys to measure the economic impact of sea-based visitors.
  • Manage the compilation of traveller contact information to facilitate International Visitor Surveys (IVS), working in close collaboration with the South Pacific Tourism Organisation (SPTO) in Suva, Fiji.
  • Coordinate with relevant line ministries and border agencies to retrieve administrative data and ensure the smooth flow of information to the TSD.
  • Perform preliminary data entry and basic cleaning of survey results to prepare them for analysis by the Economics team.
  • Assist in the logistical planning of workshops, stakeholder meetings, and technical briefings (both virtual and face-to-face).

Selection Criteria

Interested candidates should demonstrate they meet the following minimum requirements:

  • A Bachelor’s Degree or Diploma in Economics, Statistics, Tourism Management, or a related field. Minimum of one (1) year of relevant work experience for Diploma holders.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in data collection, community service, and public relations for those with a PSSC/Form 7 qualification.

The Assistant Statistician (Tourism Statistics) will be selected through the Individual Consultant Selection method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers of September 2025.

Submission Details

Expressions of Interest (EOI) must include a curriculum vitae (CV) or resume describing experience in similar assignments. EOIs MUST be received by e-mail by Friday, 13th March 2026, no later than 4:30 pm local time, clearly marked: “EOI for SICBT Assistant Statistician (Tourism Statistics) ”.

Terms of Reference (TOR) and other information will be available upon request from Ms Ana Soakai, email: asoakai@stats.gov.to or telephone 23-300/8607217.

Attention: Mr Sione Lolohea (Government Statistician), Tonga Statistics Department, 1st Floor, Si’i-Kae-Ola Supermarket Building, Taufa’ahau Road, Nuku’alofa, Tonga. Phone: +676 23-300. E-mail: sione.lolohea@stats.gov.to and copy asoakai@stats.gov.to.

CENTRAL PROJECTS COORDINATION UNIT (CPCU)
Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs

                                         The Gambia Infrastructure Project (GIP)

                   Request for Expressions of Interest for Consulting Service

 

Country: The Republic of the Gambia

Project Title: The Gambia Infrastructure Project (GIP)

Assignment Title: Consultancy for the Development of an Electricity Tariff Methodology, Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) Model, and Distributed Generation Tariff Model

Procurement Method: Consultant’s Qualification Selection Method (CQS)   

Reference No.:   GM-CPCU - MOFEA-529483-CS-CQS

Background:

The Government of the Republic of the Gambia, under the World Bank (WB) Infrastructure Project has received an IDA Grant in an indicative amount equivalent to US$52.56 million available through The Gambia’s national IDA. The bank intends to apply a portion of this grant to eligible payments under a consultancy contract for the provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of an Electricity Tariff Methodology, Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) Model, and Distributed Generation Tariff Model.

The consulting services include Consultancy for the Development of an Electricity Tariff Methodology, Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) Model, and Distributed Generation Tariff Model

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be collected from the address below or requested via email:

 

Project coordinator,

Central Project Coordination Unit,

Royal Insurance Building, OIC highway, Kotu

Email:/msanyang@cpcumof.gm /gip.procurement@cpcumof.gm / rsey@cpcumof.gm / nsosseh@cpcumof.gm  

 

The Central Project Coordination Unit – Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant Firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.:

 

  • At least 10 years of professional experience in electricity sector regulation, tariff methodology development, or utility financial modeling. 
  • Demonstrated experience in developing or revising electricity tariff methodologies and multi-year tariff (MYT) frameworks for regulatory authorities or utilities. 
  • Successful completion of at least three (3) similar assignments involving tariff reform, revenue requirement modeling, or regulatory framework development within the past ten years. 
  • Experience working with public utilities, regulatory authorities, ministries of energy, or state-owned electricity utilities. 
  • Regional and Contextual Experience 
  • Capacity Building and Knowledge Transfer
  • Project Management Capacity 

 

 

Key Staff 

The consulting team should include: 

  • Regulatory Economist / Team Leader 
  • Utility Financial Specialist / Regulatory Finance Expert 
  • Tariff Modeler / Financial Modeling Specialist 
  • Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation Specialist 

 

The attention of interested Consultant Firms are drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (July 1st, 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018 January 2020, seventh edition March 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultant Firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant Firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Selection (CQS) set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 16:00 GMT Mondays to Thursday and from 8:00am to 12:30pm GMT on Fridays.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below or by email on or before Thursday 19th March 2026 at 12:00pm GMT, to the address below clearly marked Expression of Interest for Consultancy Services for the Development of an Electricity Tariff Methodology, Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) Model, and Distributed Generation Tariff Model

Anta Taal

Project Coordinator

Central Project Coordinating Unit

Gambia Infrastructure Project (GIP)

procnotices.notice_text:
Avis d’Appel d’Offres National Ouvert N°002/AONO/MINT/ PCDN/UGP/ CSPM/2026/du 05 mars 2026 relatif à la fourniture des toxicotests et alcootests de contrôle routier

Pays : République du Cameroun

Nom du Projet : Projet régional pour l’amélioration de la performance du Corridor rail/route Douala-N’Djaména

Financement : Crédit N°70360- CM (100%)

1.La République du Cameroun ci-après dénommé l’« Emprunteur » a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet régional pour l’amélioration de la performance du Corridor rail/route Douala-N’djamena (PCDN), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché relatif à la fourniture des toxicotests et alcootests de contrôle routier. Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera la méthode de décaissement par Paiement Direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement, à l’exception des paiements pour lesquels le marché prévoit l’utilisation de crédit documentaire. 

2.Le Coordonnateur du Projet régional pour l’amélioration de la performance du Corridor rail/route Douala-N’djamena (PCDN) sollicite des offres fermées de la part des soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir des toxicotests et alcootests de contrôle routier. Il s’agit dans le cadre du présent marché de fournir mille cinq cents (1 500) toxicotests chimiques à lecture directe (pouvant détecter 11 drogues), huit (8) toxicotests électroniques (appareil de lecture), huit milles (8 000) cartouches de tests (consommables toxicotests électroniques), vingt milles (20 000) alcootests chimiques et un service connexe portant sur la formation de trente (30) utilisateurs. Le lieu de la livraison est l’Unité de Gestion du PCDN et la durée de la prestation est de trois (03) mois à compter de la notification de l’ordre de service de démarrage.

3.La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence Nationale (AON) telle que définie dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale, septième édition, septembre 2025, et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.

4.Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres.

5.Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’Unité de Gestion du PCDN, sise à Bastos, derrière l’Hôtel le Diplomate, Rue 1.904, email : claudentone@yahoo.fr avec copie à mnnjeck@gmail.com et gairamesmer@yahoo.fr et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres les jours ouvrables, de lundi à vendredi entre 08h00 et 16h00 à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessus.

6.Le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres disponible en français peut être obtenu à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessus sur présentation de la quittance de versement de la somme non remboursable de cent cinquante mille                (150 000) francs CFA. La méthode de paiement sera le virement sur le compte n° 335 988 ouvert auprès des 12 agences BICEC ci-après au nom de "Compte Spécial CAS ARMP". Il s’agit de : Agence Centrale Yaoundé, Douala Bonanjo, Buéa, Ebolowa, Dschang, Ngaoundéré, Maroua, Limbé, Bafoussam, Bamenda, Garoua et Bertoua. Le document d’appel d’offres sera adressé directement à chaque prestataire contre présentation du reçu de paiement des frais exigibles dont le montant est ci-dessus indiqué.

7.Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse suivante : Unité de Gestion du PCDN sise à Bastos, derrière l’Hôtel le Diplomate, Rue 1.904 au plus tard le 07 avril 2026 à 15 heures précises   (heure locale). La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées.  

8.Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une caution de soumission d’une durée de validité de cent vingt (120) jours, et d’un montant de quatre millions cinq cent mille (4 500 000) francs CFA, délivrée par une Banque de premier ordre ou une compagnie d’assurance agréée par le Ministère en charge des Finances. Cette caution doit être timbrée, acquittée à la main, conforme au modèle indiqué dans le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres et accompagnée d’un récépissé de consignation délivré par la Caisse des Dépôts et des Consignations.

L’absence ou la non-conformité de cette garantie de soumission timbrée à l’ouverture des plis est éliminatoire.

L’offre sera valable jusqu’au 06 juillet 2026.

9.L’attention est attirée sur le Règlement de Passation de Marchés exigeant que l’Emprunteur divulgue des informations sur la propriété effective du Soumissionnaire retenu, dans le cadre de la Notification d’Attribution du Marché, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs tel qu’il est inclus dans le document d’appel d’offres.

10.L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est :

Attention : Monsieur le Coordonnateur du Projet régional pour l’amélioration de la performance du Corridor rail/route Douala-N’Djamena.

Unité de Gestion du PCDN, sise à Bastos, derrière l’Hôtel le Diplomate, Rue 1.904

Salle de réunions située au rez-de-chaussée.

Les offres doivent être produites en huit (08) exemplaires dont un (01) original et sept (07) copies marquées comme tels, chiffrées hors taxes et toutes taxes comprises et accompagnées de la version scannée de l’original de l’offre déposée (signée et cachetée) sur clé USB.

Les enveloppes fermées devront comprendre la mention suivante :

« AVIS D’APPEL D’OFFRES NATIONAL OUVERT (AONO) N°002/AONO/MINT/ PCDN/UGP/CSPM/2026 DU 05 MARS 2026 RELATIF A LA FOURNITURE DES TOXICOTESTS ET ALCOOTESTS DE CONTROLE ROUTIER »

« - A N’OUVRIR QU’EN SEANCE DE DEPOUILLEMENT ».

                                                                        Le Coordonnateur

The consulting services (“the Services”) include conducting a comprehensive, multi-dimensional feasibility study for proposed infrastructure, site improvements, tourism facilities, and urban development interventions in the Arugam Bay and Pasikudah clusters. SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES– SELECTION OF FIRMS)

 

UGANDA RURAL ROADS PROGRAM

PROJECT ID: P182056

Procurement Reference No. MoWT/CONS/2025-2026/00502

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: Consultancy Services for Feasibility Study for the DUCAR (District, Urban and Community Access Roads) network, Bridges and Drainage Structures in 77 District Local Governments:

 

The Government of the Republic of Uganda represented by the Ministry of Works and Transport (MoWT) has received a grant of US$4,500,000 from the World Bank towards the Preparation of the Rural Roads Program and intends to apply part of the proceeds for undertaking Consultancy Services for Feasibility Study for the DUCAR network, Bridges and Drainage Structures in 77 District Local Governments. The project is spread across the 5 regions of the Country, and as such, 5 lots have been formulated as summarized below:

  1. LOT 1-West Nile Region; 12 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Adjumani, Arua, Koboko, Madi Okollo, Maracha, Moyo, Nebbi, Obongi, Pakwach, Terego, Yumbe and Zombo.
  2. LOT 2-Northern Region; 14 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Agago, Alebtong, Amolatar, Amuru, Apach, Gulu, Kitgum, Kole, Lamwo, Lira, Nwoya, Omoro, Otuke and Oyam.
  3. LOT 3-Western Region; 18 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Bundibugyo, Bushenyi, Isingiro, Kabarole, Kakumiro, Kamwenge, Kanungu, Kasese, Kibaale, Kiryandongo, Kisoro, Kitagwenda, Kyegegwa, Masindi, Mitooma, Ntoroko, Rukungiri and Sheema
  4. LOT 4-Eastern Region; 23 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Amuria, Bududa, Bugiri, Bukedea, Bukwo, Bulambuli, Busia, Butaleja, Iganga, Kaliro, Kamuli, Katakwi, Kibuuku, Kumi, Kween, Manafwa, Nabilatuk, Namayingo, Namutumba, Ngora, Pallisa, Serere and Sironko
  5. LOT 5-Central Region; 10 District Local Governments, Consisting Districts of; Buikwe, Butambala, Kalangala, Kayunga, Luwero, Mukono, Nakasongola, Rakai, Sembabule and Wakiso

The Consulting Services (“the Services”) are to be provided with the following objectives;

  1. Undertake Detailed Engineering Designs, determine an Environment and Social Management Plan, and prepare bidding documents for 1,100km of the DUCAR network, 240 bridges and drainage structures, and 50km of swamps raising in 77 District Local Governments;
  2. Undertake Economic and Financial Assessment for 1,100km of the DUCAR network, 240 bridges and drainage structures, and 50km of swamps improvement in 77 District Local Governments; and
  3. Generate a Feasibility study report for 1,100km of the DUCAR network, 240 bridges and drainage structures, and 50km of swamps in 77 District Local Governments.

The implementation period of the assignment is 6 (six) Calendar Months from the time of contract signing.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be assessed at www.mowt.go.ug.

The Ministry of Works and Transport now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

The successful execution of this consultancy requires a Consultant with extensive experience, technical competence, and proven ability to work within government and donor-funded project environments. The Consultant should combine strong analytical and facilitation skills with contextual knowledge of Uganda’s transport sector to ensure that the assessment is both practical and implementable. Specifically, the Consultant is expected to meet the following minimum requirements:

  1. Must have completed projects with a total of 100km or more for Design or Construction Supervision of Highways or Urban roads in the last 10 years;

(ii)    Experience in working with Government and Donor-funded projects; and

(iii)   Strong skills in Analysis, Reporting, and Facilitation.

 

N.B:  

  1. Firms should not bid in more than 2 (two) lots.
  2. Individual experts’ bio-data is not required at this stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”  dated February 2025 (“Procurement in Investment Project Financing: Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.

procnotices.notice_text:
SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

Pays : Burundi

Nom du Projet : Projet pour l’Emploi et la Transformation Economique (PRETE)

Numéro de Prêt/Crédit/Don:  Don IDA N° E-2650-BI

N° du projet: P172988

 

Intitule de la mission : Spécialiste en Sauvegardes Environnementales du PRETE

Numéro de référence (selon le Plan de Passation des marchés) : BI-ADB-535938-CS-INDV

La République du Burundi a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet pour l’Emploi et la Transformation Economique (PRETE), et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Spécialiste en Sauvegardes Environnementales du PRETE ».

Les services de consultants (« les services ») consistent à appuyer techniquement l’UGP du PRETE et les autres parties prenantes dans la mise en œuvre du projet dans le domaine de ses compétences. Le/la Spécialiste en Sauvegardes Environnementales du PRETE sera chargé(e) de toutes les questions relatives à la gestion des risques et impacts environnementaux du projet tels que convenus dans le Plan d’Engagement Environnemental et Social (PEES) du projet. Il/elle devra s’assurer de la prise en compte des dispositions juridiques nationales et internationales ainsi que des normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale dans la conduite des activités du PRETE.  Il/elle travaillera étroitement avec la Spécialiste en développement social, la Spécialiste en Genre et Violences Basées sur le Genre ainsi qu’en collaboration avec l’ensemble du personnel de l’UGP et les différentes parties prenantes de mise en œuvre.

La durée des prestations s’étend jusqu’à la date de clôture du Projet (29/12/2028) à partir de la notification du contrat.

Les termes de référence détaillés (TdR) pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

L’Unité de gestion du PRETE invite maintenant les candidats éligibles (« Consultants individuels ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les candidats intéressés doivent fournir toutes les informations nécessaires démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Le Consultant devra répondre aux critères suivants :

  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire de minimum Bac+4 en sciences naturelles, environnement, Biologie, Géographie, Agronomie, Gestion des écosystèmes ou dans d’autres disciplines similaires ;
  • Disposer d’une expérience professionnelle d’’au moins cinq (05) ans dans la mise en œuvre des mesures de gestion environnementale dans le secteur public ou privé. ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience dans la gestion des questions liées à l’hygiène santé et sécurité au travail ;
  • Avoir une connaissance approfondie des normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale et de la législation environnementales du Burundi ;
  • Avoir exécuté des missions similaires dans le cadre des projets financés par le Groupe de la Banque mondiale (IDA, SFI, etc.) ;
  • Une bonne connaissance des problématiques liées à la résilience climatique dans le cadre d’activités similaires à celles proposées par le projet, notamment en matière de sensibilisation du secteur public aux enjeux liés au réchauffement climatique et dans l’intégration de solutions éco-intelligentes dans le développement des chaines de valeurs serait un atout ;
  • Avoir une parfaite maîtrise du français et du Kirundi, constituent un atout ;
  • Avoir une maîtrise de l’outil informatique (Word, Excel, Power Point) ;
  • Avoir une bonne aptitude pour la communication et le travail en équipe ;
  • Être capable de travailler sous pression.

L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI » de septembre 2023 (« Règlement »), énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuels avec approche ouverte nationale, énoncée dans le Règlement de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le (FPI), Edition de septembre 2023 et conformément aux critères exigés par les termes de référence.

De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau, du Lundi au Vendredide 08 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 18 heures.

Les manifestations d'intérêt rédigées en Français et portant la mention : « Réponse à l’Avis de Sollicitation de Manifestations d'intérêt pour le recrutement d'un Spécialiste en Sauvegardes Environnementales du PRETE» doivent être remises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, ou par courrier, ou par e-mail au plus tard le 24 mars 2026 à 16 heures, heure de Bujumbura ».

Bujumbura, Burundi

REVISED REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) – EXTENSION OF THE SUBMISSION DATE

 

COUNTRY:                             Federal Government of Somalia (FGS)

NAME OF PROJECT:           Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)

Assignment Title:                    Consulting Service for Development of a Regulatory Framework for Number Portability, Short Code Guidelines, and a Model and Architecture for the Numbering Portability System

Reference No.:                         SO-MOCT-FGS-534891-CS-CQS

Place of assignment:                Mogadishu, Somalia

Original Submission Date:    March 10, 2026, at 2.00pm [Mogadishu, Somalia Local Time].

Revised Submission Date:  March 25, 2026, at 2.00pm [Mogadishu, Somalia Local Time]. 

The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) is required to be undertaken as an external consultant firm supporting to the Ministry of Communications and Technology (MOCT) in the Federal Government of Somalia to carry out the implementation of Consulting Service for Development of a Regulatory Framework for Number Portability, Short Code Guidelines, and a Model and Architecture for the Numbering Portability System. The consultant firm will undertake all the specific required tasks detailed out in the Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment. The consultancy service is expected to be conducted and reports delivered within four (4) months from commencement.     

Request for expressions of interest (REOI) can be found at the following website: https://moct.gov.so/en/jobs/ or it can be provided upon submission of application in person or by e-mail. The e-mail address is provided below.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology, FGS now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.). 

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm and at least five (5) years of proven experience in providing consultancy services related to telecommunications, legal, regulatory, and policy framework development.
  2. i) demonstrate successful completion of at least one (1) similar assignment involving the review, development, or implementation of telecommunications regulatory frameworks, including areas such as numbering, interconnection, consumer protection, competition regulation, or related Telecom regulatory domains. ii) demonstrated experience working with telecommunications regulatory authorities, with a strong understanding of regulatory processes, institutional arrangements, and the operational realities of the telecommunications sector. iii) demonstrate solid knowledge of international best practices and standards, including relevant ITU Recommendations applicable to numbering, number portability, and short code management.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES -FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Bosnia And Herzegovina

Federation of Bosnia And Herzegovina

Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs

Geospatial Infrastructure and Valuation Enhancement Project (GIVE)

Loan No.: 96760-BA

Issue date: 05.03.2026.

Assignment Title: Development of FBiH SDI data standards and model

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): A.1.2.1

 

Bosnia and Herzegovina and Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, through sub-agreement with Bosnia and Herzegovina has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Geospatial Infrastructure and Valuation Enhancement Project (GIVE), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include establishing a repeatable methodology, set of deliverables and acceptance criteria for developing, implementing, and testing spatial data models for spatial data sources of SDI stakeholders. A systematic approach to spatial data model design must be established by defining the conceptual, logical, and physical structures for the selected sources, in line with the relevant international standards (such as ISO, OGC, INSPIRE, Law on SDI FBiH) and requests from SDI stakeholders. This will lay the foundation for long-term interoperability, better organization and accessibility of stakeholder data, and strengthen the role of the SDI as a framework for the digital transformation of public administration and more effective spatial data management in the Federation of BiH.

This shall be used for contracting a Framework Agreement (FA), under which the Procuring Agency may issue multiple Call-Off Contracts/Work Orders. Each Call-Off Contract shall cover one clearly identified spatial data source (or theme) and shall be implemented through the phases and deliverables defined in Terms of Reference (ToR). For each Call-Off Contract, the Procuring Agency shall issue an Assignment Brief specifying: (i) the spatial data source/theme and responsible SDI stakeholder, (ii) available input datasets and formats, (iii) scope boundaries and assumptions, (iv) test environment and access arrangements, and (v) any source-specific constraints.

The Framework Agreement shall be concluded for a Term of 3 years, from the commencement date stated in the Framework Agreement. The initial term may be extended by a maximum of two additional years. The selection of a FA Consultant to be awarded a Call-off Contract will be done through a Secondary Procurement process as defined in Framework Agreement. However, the conclusion of a Framework Agreement shall not impose any obligation on the Procuring Agency, including participating Employers, to purchase Consulting under a Call-off Contract. The overall deadline for the Call-off Contract implementation shall be 180 calendar days from the signing of the Call-off Contract.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be found at the following website: http://fgu.com.ba/

The Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. At the initial stage, the evaluation shall be based solely on the qualifications and experience of the Consulting Firm (as an individual firm or as a joint venture/consortium). Curricula vitae (CVs) of Key Experts are not required and shall not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The maximum score is 100 points, awarded based on the cumulative assessment of the shortlisting criteria. An EoI shall be considered responsive and eligible for shortlisting only if it achieves a minimum score of fifty (50) points out of one hundred (100).

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. For JV/consortium submissions, the EoI shall clearly indicate: (i) the Lead Partner, (ii) the roles and responsibilities of each member, and  (iii) proposed coordination arrangements. Shortlisting criteria may be fulfilled cumulatively by the JV/consortium, meaning that relevant experience, references, and capacity of all JV/consortium members may be aggregated and considered in the evaluation, considering their proposed roles and responsibilities. The Lead Partner shall act as the primary point of contact for FGA. Required JV/consortium documentation (to be attached to the EoI): A signed Letter of Intent to form a JV/consortium (or equivalent written agreement) by all members, identifying the Lead Partner and confirming commitment to submit a proposal in case shortlisted; and A brief JV/consortium arrangement note describing roles, division of responsibilities, and allocation of references/experience to the proposed roles.

The shortlist will contain five (5) to eight (8) firms.

Shortlisting Criteria, Scoring and Expected Supporting Evidence (to be submitted with the EoI) are:

CRITERION 1: GENERAL EXPERIENCE (MAXIMUM 20 POINTS)

The Firm shall be awarded up to 20 points based on the quality and relevance of corporate experience and references.

  1. Minimum years in business (up to 7 points): At least two (2) years in business providing professional services in one or more of the following fields: geodesy, geoinformatics, GIS/SDI, land administration, IT/software engineering, data engineering, enterprise architecture, digital transformation, environmental information systems, utilities/asset management systems, or related fields. Expected evidence to be submitted with the EoI: Proof of legal establishment and registration (e.g., company registry extract, certificate of incorporation, or equivalent official registration document) indicating the year of establishment (for JV/consortium submissions: for each member).
  2. Core business relevance (up to 13 points): Demonstrated corporate track record in delivering assignments such as: (i) development/integration of information systems or registries; (ii) data modelling and/or standardisation (spatial or non-spatial); (iii) database development and management; (iv) interoperability, data exchange, APIs, or service-oriented architectures; (v) implementation support, documentation and/or training for enterprise systems, for public sector or regulated industries.Expected evidence to be submitted with the EoI:Firm Profile (maximum 2 pages) summarising relevant business lines and service areas; and Relevant project references documented through Project Reference Sheets and corresponding attachments (as described under Criterion 2). References may be provided cumulatively by JV/consortium members.

CRITERION 2: SPECIFIC EXPERIENCE RELEVANT TO THE ASSIGNMENT (MAXIMUM 60 POINTS)

The Firm shall be awarded up to 60 points based on the quality and relevance of project references comparable in deliverables and complexity. References may relate to geospatial SDI work or equivalent data/standards/interoperability projects in other sectors, provided that outputs are transferable to the assignment. Relevant project areas include:

  1. Data modelling / standards / interoperability specifications (up to 18 points);
  2. Standards and frameworks alignment (INSPIRE, ISO 191xx, OGC, CityGML, LADM, GML/XML, GeoPackage, or equivalent national/sectoral standards such as ISO/IEC, W3C, OpenAPI, industry reference models) (up to 14 points);
  3. Schema/API implementation and validation (XSD/JSON Schema, REST/OpenAPI, controlled vocabularies, validation workflows, QA pipelines) (up to 10 points);
  4. Database and platform implementation (spatial/enterprise DB, performance, integrity constraints, migration, ETL/ELT) (up to 10 points);
  5. Service enablement and publication (WMS/WFS/WCS, tile services, catalogues, portals, OGC API, REST services) (up to 8 points).

Expected evidence to be submitted with the EoI (mandatory format): For each reference claimed under this criterion, the Firm shall submit a Project Reference Sheet (maximum 2 pages per reference) including, at minimum: Project title; Client name and contact details; Country; Implementation period (start/end); Firm’s role (Lead / JV member / subcontractor) and brief description of scope; Key deliverables relevant to the assignment; Standards/technologies applied (where relevant); Contract value (indicative, if available). Expected reference attachments (mandatory – at least one per reference):

For each reference, the Firm shall attach at least one (1) of the following (commercially sensitive information may be redacted):

  • Contract extract / purchase order / work order evidencing the Firm’s engagement; or
  • Certificate of completion / acceptance certificate / client confirmation letter; or
  • Client reference/recommendation letter; or
  • Links or screenshots evidencing published deliverables (e.g., public documentation, geoportal/service endpoint), where applicable; or
  • Other verifiable evidence acceptable to FGA confirming participation and delivery.
  • For JV/consortium submissions, references may be submitted cumulatively by all members. Each reference sheet shall clearly indicate which member performed which part of the assignment and how it relates to the proposed role within the JV/consortium.

CRITERION 3: ADDITIONAL PREFERENTIAL CRITERIA (MAXIMUM 20 POINTS)

The Firm shall be awarded up to 20 points based on attributes that enhance implementation feasibility:

  1. Regional/BiH or comparable context experience (up to 8 points). Experience in Bosnia and Herzegovina and/or comparable contexts, or delivery of similar work for public institutions with complex governance arrangements. Expected evidence to be submitted with the EoI: Project Reference Sheets (as per Criterion 2), supported by at least one attachment per reference as listed under Criterion 2.
  2. Local capacity and language (up to 6 points). Ability to operate in Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian and deliver meetings/workshops and key documentation in local language(s). Expected evidence to be submitted with the EoI: Self-declaration confirming operational capacity in Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian; and Optional supporting evidence (recommended): sample excerpt of a prior deliverable/training agenda in local language(s) or client confirmation indicating local-language delivery.
  3. Standards/model governance and maintenance (up to 6 points). Demonstrated experience in establishing or supporting governance and maintenance arrangements for data standards and models, including change management (versioning), stakeholder review cycles, issue tracking, and publication of updated versions (e.g., model repository, registry/catalogue updates). Expected evidence to be submitted with the EoI: One (1) to two (2) Project Reference Sheets where such governance/maintenance arrangements were implemented or supported; and At least one supporting attachment per reference as defined under Criterion 2 (acceptance letter, client confirmation, or deliverable extract/link evidencing versioning/change process).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023, revised February 2023 and September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 08:00 to 16:00.

O Governo de Angola assinou um acordo de empréstimo com o Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto de Fortalecimento da Governança para a Melhoria da Prestação dos Serviços em Angola, cujos objectivos são: (i) Aumentar o montante e a fiabilidade das transferências fiscais para municípios seleccionados; (ii) reforçar a sua capacidade financeira e de gestão fundiária; (iii) aumentar a cobertura de identidade.

O projecto é multissectorial, envolvendo os seguintes Departamentos Ministeriais: Ministério das Finanças, Justiça e dos Direitos Humanos, Obras Públicas, Urbanismo e Habitação, Administração Pública, Trabalho, Segurança Social e o Ministério da Administração do Território, que tem a responsabilidade de coordenar, através de uma Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP).

O projecto terá a duração de quatro (4) anos e pretende aplicar parte deste crédito em pagamentos elegíveis para Contratação de uma firma para Serviços de Consultoria em Administração de Sistemas Windows, Linux e Serviços Geoportal SIG Web.

Os serviços de consultoria ("Serviços") incluem: definir a arquitectura de referência para servidores, serviços, utilizadores e perfis de acesso; Conceber o desenho lógico do Active Directory (domínio(s), florestas, OUs, grupos, políticas), dos serviços de e-mail institucional e do ambiente Linux de suporte a aplicações e SIG; Especificar a arquitectura do Geoportal SIG Web, incluindo camadas, serviços, perfis e regras de acesso; Propor um modelo de DevOps adaptado ao contexto do MAT; Produzir documentação técnica, planos e manuais que sirvam de guião para a implementação faseada e para a futura migração para um data center institucional. O contrato terá a duração de três (3) meses.

Os Termos de Referência (TdR) detalhados para a consultoria podem ser obtidos no endereço abaixo.

O Projecto Njila, convida agora as empresas de consultoria elegíveis ("Consultores") a manifestarem o interesse em prestar os Serviços. Os consultores interessados ​​devem fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações necessárias e a experiência relevante para a realização dos Serviços.

Os critérios de selecção para a Lista Curta são: i) A firma deverá apresentar uma equipa multidisciplinar com experiência comprovada em arquitectura de sistemas, Active Directory, ambientes Linux, SIG Web e DevOps; ii) Experiência em Angola ou em contextos similares em países de língua oficial portuguesa. Os especialistas não serão avaliados na fase de pré-selecção para a Lista Curta.

Os consultores serão avaliados com base no Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Fevereiro de 2025, pelo que deverão ter em atenção à Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16, e 3.17 das referidas Normas, que definem a política do Banco Mundial sobre o conflito de interesse. O referido documento pode ser consultado na seguinte hiperligação:https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/products-and-services/brief/procurement-new-framework.

Os consultores podem associar-se a outras empresas para melhorar as suas qualificações, mas devem indicar claramente se a associação assume a forma de uma joint venture e/ou de uma SUB consultoria. No caso de uma joint venture, todos os parceiros da joint venture serão solidariamente responsáveis pela totalidade do contrato, se selecionados.

Apenas um consultor será selecionado, através do método de Selecção Baseada na Qualidade e Custo (QCBS), em conformidade com o Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Fevereiro de 2025.

Os consultores interessados poderão obter mais informações no endereço abaixo referido, das 08:00 às 15:00, de Segunda à Sexta-Feira.

As manifestações de interesse deverão ser entregues por escrito para o endereço abaixo (pessoalmente, por correio ou e-mail) até as 15:00 horas do dia 17 de Março de 2026.

REVISED REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) – EXTENSION OF THE SUBMISSION DATE

 

COUNTRY:                             Federal Government of Somalia (FGS)

NAME OF PROJECT:           Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)  

PROJECT ID:                          P176181         

Assignment Title:                    Consulting Service for Development of Regulatory Frameworks for Infrastructure Sharing, Digital Rights of Way, Interconnection Pricing (Including Reference Interconnection Offer), and National Roaming in Somalia

Reference No.:                         SO-MOCT-FGS-534901-CS-QCBS

Place of assignment:                Mogadishu, Somalia

Original Submission Date:    March 10, 2026, at 2.00pm [Mogadishu, Somalia Local Time].

Revised Submission Date:  March 31, 2026, at 2.00pm [Mogadishu, Somalia Local Time]. 

The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) is required to be undertaken as an external consultant firm supporting to the Ministry of Communications and Technology (MOCT) in the Federal Government of Somalia to carry out the implementation of Consulting Service for Development of Regulatory Frameworks for Infrastructure Sharing, Digital Rights of Way, Interconnection Pricing (Including Reference Interconnection Offer), and National Roaming in Somalia. The consultant firm will undertake all the specific required tasks detailed out in the Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment. The consultant service is expected to be conducted and reports delivered within six (6) months from commencement.     

Request for expressions of interest (REOI) can be found at the following website: https://moct.gov.so/en/jobs/ or it can be provided upon submission of application in person or by e-mail. The e-mail address is provided below.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology, FGS now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.). 

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm and at least five (5) years of proven experience providing professional consultancy services in telecommunications regulation, legal and policy framework development, and institutional strengthening.
  2. i) demonstrate successful completion of at least one (1) similar assignment involving the assessment, development, and/or implementation of telecommunications regulatory frameworks, including but not limited to: Infrastructure sharing and wholesale access; Digital or telecommunications rights of way; Interconnection pricing and reference interconnection offers (RIO); National roaming, competition regulation, numbering, or related regulatory domains. ii) demonstrated experience working with telecommunications regulatory authorities or relevant government institutions, including a clear understanding of: Regulatory processes and legal mandates; Stakeholder consultation and validation procedures; Enforcement, compliance monitoring, and dispute resolution mechanisms. iii) demonstrate strong technical, economic, and legal expertise relevant to the development of operational and enforceable regulatory instruments, including Cost-oriented pricing and simplified costing methodologies; Drafting of regulations, guidelines, and model agreements; Development of implementation toolkits, templates, and regulatory roadmaps.
  3. Experience of relevant services in an environment similar to that of Somalia; and
  4. The technical and managerial organization of the firm. (Provide only the structure of the organization. (Do not provide CVs of staff). Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint venture and/ or a Sub consultancy. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality And Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

REPÚBLICA DE ANGOLA

País: Angola.

Nome do Projecto: Projecto Njila.

ID do Projecto N. º P178040.

Descrição do Contrato: Contratação de uma firma para elaboração de Guias práticos sobre a gestão Autárquica.

Não. do Contrato: 50/C2/C/PROFOGMEPS/23

O Governo de Angola assinou um acordo de empréstimo com o Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto de Fortalecimento da Governança para a Melhoria da Prestação dos Serviços em Angola, cujos objectivos são: (i) Aumentar o montante e a fiabilidade das transferências fiscais para municípios selecionados; (ii) reforçar a sua capacidade financeira e de gestão fundiária; (iii) aumentar a cobertura de identidade.

O projecto é multissectorial, envolvendo os seguintes Departamentos Ministeriais: Ministério das Finanças, Justiça e dos Direitos Humanos, Obras Públicas, Urbanismo e Habitação, Administração Pública, Trabalho, Segurança Social e o Ministério da Administração do Território, que tem a responsabilidade de coordenar, através de uma Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP).

O projecto terá a duração de quatro (4) anos e pretende aplicar parte deste crédito em pagamentos elegíveis para Contratação de uma firma para elaboração de Guias práticos sobre a gestão Autárquica.

Os serviços de consultoria ("Serviços") incluem: Identificação do público-alvo dos Guias práticos e a definição dos assuntos a serem abordados; Elaboração de um plano de comunicação e estrutura dos Guias práticos; Aumentar a Cobertura de Identidade para Permitir o Acesso Inclusivo aos Serviços; Criação de conteúdo informativo e educativo de acordo com as boas práticas de comunicação; Revisão e edição do conteúdo para garantir clareza, precisão e relevância; Design gráfico e layout da cartilha para torná-la visualmente atractiva e acessível; Revisão final e produção dos Guias Práticos em formato impresso e/ou digital; Formação e capacitação da equipa do MAT na utilização e divulgação dos Guias Práticos público-alvo. O contrato terá a duração de três (3) meses.

Os Termos de Referência (TdR) detalhados para a consultoria podem ser obtidos no endereço abaixo.

O Projecto Njila, convida agora as empresas de consultoria elegíveis ("Consultores") a manifestarem o interesse em prestar os Serviços. Os consultores interessados devem fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações necessárias e a experiência relevante para a realização dos Serviços.

Os critérios de selecção para a Lista Curta são: i) Pelo menos 5 anos de experiência comprovada na elaboração de materiais educativos e informativos para órgãos autárquicos ou da Administração Local do Estado; ii) Experiência em Angola ou em contextos similares em países de língua oficial portuguesa; iii) Capacidade para realizar pesquisas detalhadas sobre o tema da Gestão Autárquica, bem como habilidade na produção de conteúdo relevante e de qualidade para os Guias práticos. Os especialistas não serão avaliados na fase de pré-selecção para a Lista Curta.

Os consultores serão avaliados com base no Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Fevereiro de 2025, pelo que deverão ter em atenção à Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16, e 3.17 das referidas Normas, que definem a política do Banco Mundial sobre o conflito de interesse. O referido documento pode ser consultado na seguinte hiperligação:https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/products-and-services/brief/procurement-new-framework.

Os consultores podem associar-se a outras empresas para melhorar as suas qualificações, mas devem indicar claramente se a associação assume a forma de uma joint venture e/ou de uma SUB consultoria. No caso de uma joint venture, todos os parceiros da joint venture serão solidariamente responsáveis pela totalidade do contrato, se selecionados.

Apenas um consultor será selecionado, através do método de Selecção Baseada na Qualidade e Custo (QCBS), em conformidade com o Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Fevereiro de 2025.

Os consultores interessados poderão obter mais informações no endereço abaixo referido, das 08:00 às 15:00, de Segunda à Sexta-Feira.

As manifestações de interesse deverão ser entregues por escrito para o endereço abaixo (pessoalmente, por correio ou e-mail) até as 15:00 horas do dia 17 de Março de 2026.

Request for Expressions of Interest

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Communication Officer

Project Name

Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project

Project Number

P502591

https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P502591

Activity and Reference Number (STEP)

Communication Officer (PO) FJ-PIFS-538053-CS-INDV

Implementing Agency Names

Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat

Country

FIJI

The Pacific Island Forum Secretariat (PIFS) and seven pacific island member countries (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) have received financing (grants and credits) from the World Bank (WB) Group’s International Development Association (IDA) towards the “Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project” (the Project) and will apply part of these proceeds to the contract below for Consulting Services.

The PIFS is seeking a qualified and experienced national Communications Officer to provide support to PMU and participating countries by developing high-quality knowledge and information products, including the translation of research and highly technical outputs into clear, concise, and visually engaging formats.

The Officer will work closely with the Project Coordinator and the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist to ensure that project interventions and impacts are communicated clearly to all stakeholder types. This is a full-time work assignment at PMU housed within the PIF office in Suva. In line with the project timeline, the engagement will initially be for two (2) years with an extension of a further two years (based on consultant’s performance evaluations and project needs). 

Under the overall direction of the Project Coordinator, the Communication Officer shall undertake the following activities:

Communications Strategy

  • Develop and implement the project communications strategy.
  • Develop communication materials, including press releases, brochures, presentations and social media content.

 

Media Relations

  • Establish and maintain relationships with local, national, regional and international media.
  • Disseminate project information and achievements through press releases, media advisories and targeted media outreach.
  • Facilitate media coverage of project events and activities.

 

 

Stakeholder Engagement and Missions

  • Develop and implement stakeholder engagement plans, including communication strategies for different stakeholder groups.
  • Maintain master list of all project stakeholders (internal and external).
  • Conduct missions to collect stakeholder and beneficiary feedback to inform knowledge and communication products.
  • Liaise with PMU country coordinators to identify and document project progress and challenges.

 

Knowledge, Communication and Information Products

  • Support the development and production of a wide range of knowledge, communication, and information products, including research summaries, results reports, policy briefs, press releases, blog posts, case studies, talking points, speeches, social media content, brochures, flyers, news releases, mission briefs, project and country profiles, and presentations.

 

Events Management

  • Support the organization and promotion of project events and workshops such as webinars, forums, meetings, consultations etc. This includes the development of communication materials for events including invitations, agenda, presentations, panel moderation, event facilitation, speaking and briefing notes as well as panel moderation and event facilitation.

 

Monitoring and Reporting

  • Support the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist by translating project data into knowledge and information products for various audiences.
  • Report on communication activities to the PMU.

 

Branding and Visibility

  • Ensure consistent branding and messaging across all communication materials.
  • Promote the project’s visibility through various communications channels

Applicants will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

Mandatory Criteria

Description

Education

A bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, media, or a related field.

Experience

Minimum of 5 years work experience supporting development initiatives for donor funded programmes in the Pacific. 

Evaluated Criteria:

Evaluated Criteria

Points

Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing communications and project visibility strategies for donor funded projects in the Pacific

 30

Demonstrated experience in media relations and events management

30

Experience with data visualisation or document design tools (e.g., Excel, PowerPoint, Canva) -

20

Familiarity with financial sector development, cross-border payments, or financial inclusion

20

PIFS, on behalf of the participating member countries, now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae and a cover letter with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.).

Firms’ staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated February 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached below and provides details of the scope of the services required along with specific deliverables expected. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09.00 to 17.00 hrs Fiji Time.

Terms of Reference

Communications Officer

 

Project Background

The objective of the CBR project is to ensure continuous access to correspondent banking services for participating Pacific Island Countries (PICs) while improving the enabling environment and fostering regulatory harmonization. The project is implemented by a Project Management Unit (PMU) with financial and technical support from the World Bank. The project was approved by the World Bank in August 2024, declared effective April 2025, and has a 6-year implementation period, with project ending 2030. 

The Pacific Island Forum Secretariat (PIFS) and eight pacific island member countries (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) have received financing (grants and credits) from the World Bank (WB) Group’s International Development Association (IDA) towards the “Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project” (the Project) and will apply part of these proceeds to the contract below for Consulting Services. The PIFS is the Implementing Agency for the regional project.

The Communications Officer will support the PMU and participating countries by developing high-quality knowledge and information products, including the translation of research and highly technical outputs into clear, concise, and visually engaging formats. The knowledge and information products will be used to inform policy, advocacy and awareness as well as strategic engagement. The Officer will work closely with the Project Coordinator and the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist to ensure that project interventions and impacts are communicated clearly to all stakeholder types.

PIFS now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

Objective of the Position

The Communications Officer will support the Project Management Unit (PMU) will be responsible for developing and implementing the communications and visibility of the project. The strategy should enhance visibility, promote stakeholder engagement and facilitate knowledge management.

Scope of Services

The Officer will be required to:

Communications Strategy

  • Develop and implement the project communications strategy.
  • Develop communication materials, including press releases, brochures, presentations and social media content.

Media Relations

  • Establish and maintain relationships with local, national, regional and international media.
  • Disseminate project information and achievements through press releases, media advisories and targeted media outreach.
  • Facilitate media coverage of project events and activities.

 

Stakeholder Engagement and Missions

  • Develop and implement stakeholder engagement plans, including communication strategies for different stakeholder groups.
  • Maintain master list of all project stakeholders (internal and external).
  • Conduct missions to collect stakeholder and beneficiary feedback to inform knowledge and communication products.
  • Liaise with PMU country coordinators to identify and document project progress and challenges.

 

Knowledge, Communication and Information Products

  • Support the development and production of a wide range of knowledge, communication, and information products, including research summaries, results reports, policy briefs, press releases, blog posts, case studies, talking points, speeches, social media content, brochures, flyers, news releases, mission briefs, project and country profiles, and presentations.

 

Events Management

  • Support the organization and promotion of project events and workshops such as webinars, forums, meetings, consultations etc. This includes the development of communication materials for events including invitations, agenda, presentations, panel moderation, event facilitation, speaking and briefing notes as well as panel moderation and event facilitation.

 

Monitoring and Reporting

  • Support the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist by translating project data into knowledge and information products for various audiences.
  • Report on communication activities to the PMU.

 

Branding and Visibility

  • Ensure consistent branding and messaging across all communication materials.
  • Promote the project’s visibility through various communications channels

 

Reporting Obligations

The Communications Officer will report to the PMU Project Coordinator and work in close collaboration with the M&E Specialist, the broader PMU Team and the PIFS Communications team.

 

Qualifications and Experience

Mandatory

  • A bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, media, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 5 years work experience supporting development initiatives for donor funded programmes in the Pacific. 

 

 

Desirable

  • Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing communications and project visibility strategies for donor funded projects in the Pacific
  • Demonstrated experience in media relations and events management   
  • experience with data visualisation or document design tools (e.g., Excel, PowerPoint, Canva)
  • Familiarity with financial sector development, cross-border payments, or financial inclusion
  • Experience working with regional organisations, multilateral development banks, or donor-funded programmes/projects in the Pacific.

.

Institutional Arrangements

The Officer will be provided with office space, computer, internet, and communications facilities by the PIFS. Some travel to participating countries may be required. The Officer is expected to observe confidentiality requirements and adhere to all PIFS policies, including its conflict of interest and anti-corruption guidelines.

 

Selection Process

Selection will follow the World Bank Procurement Regulations for Individual Consultants. Shortlisted candidates may be required to undergo an interview and/or written test. At least two professional references must be provided.

 

PIFS is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Applications from women, persons with disabilities, and people from diverse backgrounds are strongly encouraged.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the recruitment of the Administration Officer, among others. The overall responsibility of the officer is to:

procnotices.notice_text:
Invitations for Expression of Interest

Assignment Title:

Assistant Statistician – Data Collection (3 positions for Price Surveys)

Name of Project:

Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in Tonga (SICBT)

Grant No:

D543-TO

Date of Issuance:

Friday, 6th March 2026

Market Approach:

Open for Tongan Nationals Only

Due date/time for Expression of Interest (EOI): Friday, 13th March 2026, no later than 4:30 pm local time.

The Government of Tonga has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in Tonga (SICBT) Project. The Tonga Statistics Department is the Implementing Agency and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the recruitment of three (3) Assistant Statisticians – Data Collection.  

The primary objective of the three Assistant Statisticians is to provide essential support to the Economics team in collecting, processing, and compiling key economic statistics. These officers will assist in conducting the regular economic surveys required to establish and maintain the Building Material Price Index (BMPI), the Producer Price Index (PPI), and the Cost of Living Index.

  • Duration: Short-term position for 6 months, including a 1-month probationary period.
  • Tentative Start Date: 18 March 2026.
  • Location: The Assistant will be based at the TSD office in Nuku’alofa, Tonga.

The Assistant Statisticians will work under the management of the Head of Economics and TSD staff to:

  • Prepare and distribute survey questionnaires and data collection instruments.
  • Conduct follow-up communications with respondents to ensure timely data submission.
  • Maintain and update physical and electronic economic statistics databases.
  • Assist in quality assurance and validation to identify data inconsistencies or errors.
  • Prepare preliminary tables, charts, and graphs for economic indicators and reports.
  • Provide administrative support for workshops, meetings, and fieldwork activities.

Selection Criteria

Interested candidates should demonstrate they meet the following minimum requirements:

Academic Background and Relevant Experience

  • A Bachelor’s Degree or Diploma in Economics, Statistics or a related field. Minimum of one (1) year of relevant work experience for Diploma holders.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in data collection, community service, and public relations for those with a PSSC/Form 7 qualification.

Competencies

  • Good analytical skills - identifying price changes, verifying outliers, and ensuring data consistency
  • Computer literate with good skills in common software such as Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint).
  • Good communication skills; fluent in English and Tongan, both written and spoken language

Personal Attributes

  • Result-oriented, proactive, and highly motivated.  
  • Honesty and integrity.
  • Innovative and positively addresses change.
  • Accountable and responsible.
  • Good teamwork, collaboration skills and committed to the task at hand.

The Assistant Statistician will be selected through the Individual Consultant Selection method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers of September 2025.

Terms of Reference (TOR) and other information will be available upon request from Ms Ana Soakai, email: asoakai@stats.gov.to or telephone 23-300/8607217.

Submission Details

Expressions of Interest (EOI) must include a curriculum vitae (CV) or resume describing experience in similar assignments. EOIs MUST be received by e-mail by Friday, 13th March 2026, no later than 4:30 pm local time, clearly marked: “EOI for Assistant Statistician – Data Collection”.

Attention:

Mr Sione Lolohea (Government Statistician)

Tonga Statistics Department

1st Floor Si’i-Kae-Ola Supermarket Building

Taufa’ahau Road, Nuku’alofa, Tonga

Phone: +676 23-300

E-mail: sione.lolohea@stats.gov.to and Copy to asoakai@stats.gov.to.

 

 

 

Invitations for Expression of Interest

Assignment Title:

Assistant Statistician – Data Collection (1 position for Historical Documentation & Research)

Name of Project:

Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in Tonga (SICBT)

Grant No:

D543-TO

Date of Issuance:

Friday, 6th March 2026

Market Approach:

Open for Tongan Nationals Only

Due date/time for Expression of Interest (EOI): Friday, 13th March 2026, no later than 4:30 pm local time.

The Government of Tonga has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in Tonga (SICBT) Project. The Tonga Statistics Department is the Implementing Agency and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the recruitment of an Assistant Statistician – Data Collection.

The objective of the recruitment of the Assistant Statistician – Data Collection for Historical Documentation & Research is to provide specialised research and qualitative data support to the Tonga Statistics Department (TSD).  The individual will be responsible for identifying founding pioneers, tracing ministerial leadership, and documenting the evolution of the department’s approved budget since its inception. This work will culminate in the assembly of primary source materials to produce a commemorative book or booklet celebrating the 70th anniversary of Tonga’s Population Census.

  • Duration: Short-term position for 6 months, including a 1-month probationary period.
  • Tentative Start Date: 18 March 2026.
  • Location: The Assistant will be based at the TSD office in Nuku’alofa, Tonga.

The Assistant Statisticians will work under the management of the Government Statistician and the Project Coordinator to:

  • Conduct comprehensive reviews of historical records to identify the founders and original staff of the Statistics Office.
  • Trace and document the chronological lineage of Ministers responsible for the Department since its implementation.
  • Research and compile a record of the approved annual budgets for the office from its inception to the present day.
  • Draft structured interview questions and guides tailored for key stakeholders, including retired staff and former government officials.
  • Organise and conduct one-on-one interviews and focus group discussions to capture oral histories and institutional memory.
  • Synthesise collected qualitative and quantitative data into a cohesive narrative for the commemorative booklet.
  • Maintain and update a dedicated electronic and physical filing system for all historical research materials.
  • Assist in the quality assurance and validation of historical facts and figures to ensure accuracy in the final publication.
  • Provide administrative and logistical support for workshops or meetings related to the 70th-anniversary project.
  • Coordinate with other government divisions for data sharing and the verification of historical records.

 

Selection Criteria

Interested candidates should demonstrate they meet the following minimum requirements:

Academic Background and Relevant Experience

  • A minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree in Economics, Statistics, History, Communications, or a related Social Science field.
  • At least two (2) years of relevant work experience in research, qualitative data collection, or archival documentation.
  • Must possess exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with a proven ability to conduct high-level interviews and facilitate focus group discussions.

Competencies

  • Exceptional verbal and written communication; must be fully fluent in both English and Tongan.
  • Strong ability to synthesise historical and financial data into a cohesive narrative.
  • Computer literate with good skills in common software such as Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint).
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) for documenting research findings.
  • Proactive, highly motivated, and able to maintain good public relations and teamwork.

Personal Attributes

  • High level of honesty and integrity, especially when handling sensitive historical or financial records.
  • Result-oriented and responsible for meeting project deadlines.
  • Strong teamwork skills to coordinate effectively within the TSD team.

Selection Method

  • The Assistant Statistician will be selected through the “Individual Consultant Selection method” in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations) of September 2025.

.

Terms of Reference (TOR) and other information will be available upon request from Ms Ana Soakai, email: asoakai@stats.gov.to or telephone 23-300/8607217.
